q: 1. Permeability of soil varies
options: inversely as square of grain size
explain: From Hazen's/Kozeny-type relations (k = C·D10²), coefficient of permeability is proportional to the square of the effective grain size.

q: 2. The coefficient of permeability is proportional to void ratio (e) as K = 100 D10² i.e., K ∝ D10²
explain: The Kozeny-Carman equation shows permeability is proportional to the function e³/(1+e), which accounts for void ratio's effect on flow paths.

q: 3. The soil moisture driven off by heat, is called
explain: Hygroscopic (adsorbed) water is held tightly around particles by molecular attraction and is removed only by heating (oven drying), unlike free/gravity water.

q: 4. The capillary rise of water
options: increases as the size of the soil particles increases
decreases as the size of the soil particles decreases
is less in wet soil than in dry soil
explain: Capillary rise is governed by surface tension forces (menisci) at the air-water interface within the pores; hence it fundamentally depends on the responsible surface-tension force, and inversely on pore size.

q: 5. The phreatic line in an earth dam may be
explain: The top flow line (phreatic line) of seepage through an earth dam closely approximates a parabola (Casagrande's basic parabola method).

q: 6. The ratio of settlement at any time 't' to the final settlement, is known as
explain: Degree of consolidation U = settlement at time t / ultimate (final) settlement, a dimensionless fraction describing consolidation progress.

q: 7. One dimensional theory of Consolidation of Terzaghi is based on the assumption that
options: excess water is drained out only in the vertical direction
head is applied in one direction
explain: Terzaghi's 1-D consolidation theory assumes constant permeability, purely vertical drainage, and one-directional head/flow — all these assumptions together define the theory.

q: 8. Active earth pressure is
options: always less than passive earth pressure
always greater than passive earth pressure
sometimes greater than passive earth pressure
explain: Since active pressure coefficient Ka = (1-sinφ)/(1+sinφ) is always less than passive coefficient Kp = (1+sinφ)/(1-sinφ), active pressure is always less than passive pressure.

q: 9. When the steady seepage occurs in an isotropic soil, the head causing the flow satisfies the following equation .............
explain: Steady seepage through an isotropic, homogeneous soil is governed by Laplace's equation, the basis for flow net construction.

q: 10. In Mohr's stress circle, the co-ordinates of the center of the circle are
explain: Mohr's circle has its centre on the normal-stress axis at the average of major and minor principal stresses, i.e., ((σ1+σ3)/2, 0).

q: 11. In a flownet, which of the following statement is true?
options: Flow lines and equipotential lines intersect at oblique angles
Flow lines and equipotential lines intersect orthogonally
Flow rate through each flow channel is different
The head along each flow line is constant
explain: By construction, flow lines and equipotential lines in a properly drawn flow net always intersect at right angles (orthogonally).

q: 12. The permeability of a soil deposit-in-situ can be best obtained by .............
explain: A field pumping test captures the actual in-situ permeability of a soil deposit, accounting for natural heterogeneity that lab tests cannot.

q: 13. Over-consolidation may be due to .............
options: the weight of ice sheet or glacier which is melted away
weight of the land side which is removed
explain: Over-consolidation results from removal of a previously applied overburden, whether from a melted glacier or an eroded/removed landmass — both mechanisms apply.

q: 14. Bleeder wells are required to .............
explain: Bleeder wells relieve excess pore water pressure trapped beneath impervious layers, preventing uplift or blowout.

q: 15. Taylor's stability number is equal to Sn = c/(PHc) = c/(PH×FOS). For Hc, FOS=1
explain: When FOS = 1 (i.e., the critical/failure condition), the stability number simplifies to Sn = c/Hc, using the critical height Hc directly.

q: 16. A plate load test is useful to estimate
options: Both bearing capacity and settlement of foundation
explain: The plate load test provides a load-settlement curve from which both the safe bearing capacity and the expected settlement of the actual foundation can be estimated.

q: 17. The expression for critical gradient is .............
explain: Critical hydraulic gradient is derived by equating upward seepage force to submerged weight: ic = (G-1)/(1+e).

q: 18. Graphical method for the determination of earth pressure
explain: Culmann's graphical method is a well-known trial-wedge construction technique for determining active/passive earth pressure, especially for irregular backfill conditions.

q: 19. The value of coefficient of permeability of clays is .............
explain: Clays, with their very fine pores, have extremely low permeability, typically less than 10^-6 cm/s.

q: 20. The angle that Coulomb's failure envelope makes with the horizontal is called
explain: In a Mohr-Coulomb shear strength plot, the slope of the failure envelope line with the horizontal (normal stress) axis is the angle of internal friction, φ.

q: 21. The angle between the abscissa and the tangent to the curve representing the relationship of shearing resistance to normal stress acting within a soil is called
explain: The slope of the shear stress vs normal stress curve (Mohr-Coulomb envelope) with the horizontal axis is, by definition, the angle of internal friction.

q: 22. The constant of proportionality between seepage velocity and hydraulic gradient is called .............
explain: Seepage (percolation) velocity relates to hydraulic gradient through the coefficient of percolation, which uses the net (void) cross-sectional area.

q: 23. The zone of soil mass above the water table which is saturated by capillary moisture is called .............
explain: The capillary fringe is the zone directly above the water table kept saturated by capillary action.

q: 24. Hydraulic gradient provided at the downstream side of a hydraulic structures such as dam is called
explain: The hydraulic gradient at the point where seepage water exits the ground on the downstream side of a dam/structure is called the exit gradient, critical for piping/uplift checks.

q: 25. Falling head permeability test is preferable when soil sample is
explain: The falling head test suits fine-grained soils (clays) with low permeability, where the small, slow water flow can be accurately measured by the falling head in a standpipe, unlike the constant head test used for sandy soils.

q: 26. A soil which does not permit the passage or seepage of any permeant through its voids, is known as .............
explain: A soil that blocks all seepage flow through its voids is, by definition, an impermeable soil.

q: 27. Consolidation is a process involving
explain: Consolidation is defined by the slow, time-dependent, gradual expulsion of pore water from saturated soil under sustained load, not sudden or abnormal effects.

q: 28. The maximum size of plate for plate load test is
explain: As per standard plate load test procedure, the test plate size typically ranges up to about 60 cm (square/circular), used to simulate the foundation's bearing behaviour.

q: 29. Expansion of soils under shear is known as .............
explain: Dilatancy is the tendency of dense granular soils to expand in volume when subjected to shear.

q: 30. Coefficient of permeability of a soil .............
options: increases with the decrease in temperature
increases with the increase in temperature
explain: Permeability increases with temperature because higher temperature reduces water's viscosity, allowing easier flow.

q: 31. The value of Reynold's number for laminar flow through soil is .............
explain: Flow through soil is generally laminar as long as the Reynolds number stays below about 2,000, well within Darcy's law's valid range.

q: 32. Permeability of soil varies .............
options: inversely as square of grain size
explain: Per typical permeability relations (e.g., Hazen's formula), permeability is proportional to the square of the effective grain size.

q: 33. The equi-potential line in a seepage through a soil medium is defined as the .............
options: path of particles of water through a saturated soil mass
line connecting points of equal head of water
flow of movement of fine particles of soil
explain: An equipotential line connects all points in the seepage domain that share the same total head.

q: 34. Rise in the water table position upto the ground surface causes .............
explain: A rising water table increases pore water pressure and total stress at a given point, while effective stress typically decreases due to buoyant unit weight replacing dry/moist unit weight.

q: 35. Electrical analogy method is used to .............
options: find the depth to water table
find the water content in a soil
explain: The electrical analogy method uses the similarity between Darcy's and Ohm's laws to experimentally construct flow nets.

q: 36. Find out the correct statement about shape factor .............
explain: The shape factor of a flow net depends only on geometry, not on the permeability value of the soil.

q: 37. The pheriatic line is .............
options: the u/s face of the earth dam
d/s face of the earth dam
explain: The phreatic line is defined as the top flow line (free surface) of seepage through an earth dam.

q: 38. Quick sand is .............
options: a condition in which cohesion is decreased quickly
a sand which can act as a quick filter
condition in which cohesion less soil looses its shear strength due to upward flow of water
explain: Quicksand describes the condition where upward seepage force equals or exceeds submerged weight, eliminating effective stress and shear strength in cohesionless soil.

q: 39. Flow net consists of a number of stream lines and equipotential lines which are .............
explain: Flow lines and equipotential lines in a flow net are drawn orthogonal (at right angles) to each other by construction.

q: 40. The seepage force in soils at exit is proportional to .............
options: the head of water at d/s
the head of water at u/s
explain: Seepage force per unit volume at the exit point is directly proportional to the exit hydraulic gradient.

q: 41. Generally, when compacted the GW type of soils will be .............
explain: Even when well compacted, well-graded gravel (GW) retains interconnected voids large enough to remain pervious.

q: 42. As the length of drainage path increases the time required for consolidation .............
explain: Since time factor Tv = Cv.t/d^2, a longer drainage path (d) requires proportionally more time (as d^2) to reach the same degree of consolidation.

q: 43. In the case of stratified soils, the permeabilities Kx and Kz along and across stratification are related as .............
options: no relation between Kx and Kz
explain: Stratified soils have higher permeability parallel to layering (Kx, horizontal) than across it (Kz, vertical), since flow along layers avoids crossing low-permeability lenses.

q: 44. In the Terzaghi's theory of one dimensional consolidation it is assumed that .............
options: coefficient of volume change is not constant
explain: A core assumption of Terzaghi's theory is that both flow and compression occur strictly in one dimension (vertical).
